links.title: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python, 3rd edition: Chapter 23, Controlling the Keyboard and Mouse
links.why: The course textbook's own chapter, free online: coordinates, mouse and keyboard calls, screenshots, windows and the practice programs.

links.title: Welcome to PyAutoGUI's documentation
links.why: The library's own overview: what it can do, the spiral example, the FAQ (primary monitor only, no OCR) and the fail-safe.

links.title: Mouse Control Functions
links.why: Coordinates, onScreen(), moveTo() with None, clicks, drags, tweening and scrolling, with the exact arguments.

links.title: Keyboard Control Functions
links.why: write(), press(), hold(), hotkey() and the full KEYBOARD_KEYS list of key names.

links.title: Screenshot Functions
links.why: screenshot(), the locate functions, the order in which they search and ImageNotFoundException.

links.title: Message Box Functions
links.why: alert(), confirm(), prompt() and password(): what each shows and returns.

links.title: Cheat Sheet
links.why: One page of the whole API: PAUSE, FAILSAFE, mouse, keyboard, message boxes and screenshots.

links.title: MouseInfo documentation
links.why: The small program that shows pointer coordinates and pixel colours, to plan a script's positions.

links.title: PyScreeze README (raw text)
links.why: The module behind the screenshot, pixel and locate functions, and the helper programs it needs on Linux.

links.title: PyGetWindow README (raw text)
links.why: The window functions and the statement that only Windows is implemented.

links.title: Pyperclip README (raw text)
links.why: copy() and paste(), and the xclip or xsel programs Linux needs.

links.title: collections: Container datatypes
links.why: namedtuple, the type behind Size, Point and Box.

links.title: Logging HOWTO
links.why: How to log a script's steps to a file with the logging module.

links.title: Getting started | Selenium
links.why: What WebDriver is, for practice question 10 (PyAutoGUI or Selenium for a web browser).

_note: Every url was opened on the date in 'checked' (fetched with curl through the session proxy) and its content read; titles are those of the pages, except for the three README links, which are raw text files without a page title and are named for their project. The Python documentation pages served on that date were headed Python 3.14.8, while the study ran Python 3.14.4. The GitHub repository pages of PyScreeze, PyGetWindow, Pyperclip and sushigoroundbot and the PyPI project pages were not listed because the repository pages returned an access error and the PyPI pages a browser challenge. No video or discussion thread is listed: none was opened and read.
